newsitem.title: USA: Cerner spurns suitors, buys time for business plan.
newsitem.headline: Cerner spurns suitors, buys time for business plan.

text.p: Cerner Corp, fending off unsolicited merger overtures with a new shareholder rights plan, is buying time to prove its value as an independent company, analysts said Friday.

"They want to prove they can be worth more as an independent than as a subsidiary of another company," Kevin Dyches, an analyst at George K. Baum & Co, said. "This shareholder rights plan could buy them the time they need to pull that off."

Cerner, a provider of health care information services, said Thursday it received several unsolicited inquiries and proposals on an acquisition or merger. Cerner also authorized the repurchase of up to $25 million in common stock.

The Kansas City-based company's board launched the anti-takeover provision and a stock repurchase program, saying that "Cerner is strongly committed to fulfilling the company's long term strategy and believe any business combination at this time would deprive stockholders of the long-term value expected...as a result of implementing this strategy."
HBO & Co, Shared Medical Systems Inc and IBM Corp might be interested in Cerner, analysts said. The firms were unavailable for comment. Cerner had no comment.

A key element in Cerner's strategy is the success of its new Health Network Architecture 500 software upgrade, which helps hospitals and clinics automate their clinical, operational and management functions, analysts said.
"We're installing the new software (HNA 500) with our partner, hopefully with as many of our existing clients as possible by the end of the year," Wendy Coffey, a Cerner spokeswoman, said.
Coffey declined to specify how many clients would receive the upgrade, although she said 30 so-called beta clients will use the HNA 500 system through 1997.
How well the HNA 500 rollout works could determine whether Cerner's recent efforts to recover from a string of earnings shortfalls will pay off, analysts said.

Cerner, which reported a 78-percent drop in third-quarter earnings to $770,000 in October, said it was having trouble closing deals being made by its expanded sales staff. Revenues in the period were actually up four percent at $43.4 million.

"The company's value is in the completion of the software upgrade," said John Penshorn, an analyst at Piper Jaffray Cos. "If Cerner was taken over today, the buyer wouldn't want to pay a premium for software that's not complete. And if they complete it and sales rise, why would they sell?"
"The shareholder rights plan and stock buyback is a message to customers and sales staff that Cerner will be around for the long term," Penshorn said.

Dyches said the rise in Cerner stock Friday does not reflect the likelihood the company will be acquired. "The market is excited they may be selling, but I don't think they want to sell." Cerner stock rose 2-3/4 to 14.
